sim.inplane_count_floor_fraction

positivity guard, not physics: no face may fall below this fraction of the count it was built with, because a face whose reference area reaches zero has no tension law left. Enforced by scaling each edge's one antisymmetric flux with its donor face's allowance, so the guard cannot create or destroy material the way clipping each face after the update would. One starved face therefore does not freeze the whole sheet. A run that reaches the floor is a run whose redistribution was limited, and the minimum donor allowance is in the record; it is not a failure of the step.

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.0510.001–0.5example
sim.inplane_flow_cg_iters

numerical CAP, not physics and not the expected count: the most Jacobi-PCG updates the backward-Euler edge solve of physics.surface_count_flow may spend in one step. The solve stops on its own criterion (no face count wrong by one unit of material: ||r||_2 <= 1/(dt sqrt(6) c_max), module docstring 'Convergence'), warm-started from the last flux where that start is nearer; a step that reaches this cap first is recorded as under-solved (report solve_cap_hit = 1, with solve_defect_norm against solve_stop_norm), never rejected. The launches are fixed (no host read inside the step), so a converged solve spends the remainder as device no-ops. 4096 = 2 x the CG Chebyshev bound 0.5 sqrt(kappa) ln(2/eps) at the finest swept spacing (resolution.spacing 0.05 um; kappa <= 1 + 6 dt c g ~ 4.1e4 at dt 1e-2, eps ~ 3e-9 on a 7.5 um GUV) ~ 2.1e3; the host mirror needed 787 cold updates on a 0.07 um GUV icosphere with 1 % count noise. Conservation of the total count does not depend on this number (the unknown is the per-edge flux and every edge hands its two faces the same value with opposite signs); an under-solved step redistributes LESS, never more or from nowhere. The per-step record reports aggregate count/conservation and solve diagnostics; the per-face count and the warm-start flux are declared dynamic provider state, but continuation still requires recorder integration and a verified restore.

sim.face_area_penalty_increment

Numerical continuation increment in units of the reference penalty per ALM round. Unit ramp is an explicit solver example, not fitted to device measurements; sweep from constant penalty (0) to adding one reference penalty per round (1). With the existing 10 rounds, scale is 1 through 10, not a new iteration cap. No area tolerance, multiplier convergence test or threshold added. Host algebra: error contraction K/(K+A0*rho_j) for an affine area constraint and SPD quadratic; not a general convergence guarantee for inexact/nonconvex U1 solves.

contact.kappa

barrier stiffness of b(d) = -kappa (d - d_hat)^2 ln(d/d_hat) (energy/sdf.py, energy/barrier.py). It pushes back with |b'(d_hat/2)| = kappa d_hat (ln 2 + 1/2), so kappa = F_hold / (d_hat (ln 2 + 1/2)) holds F_hold at half the activation distance: F_hold = 100 pN is a number stated here, not a row (the order of the largest bond force of the lane build, as the Lead gave it 2026-09-24 00:2x; not re-measured), and d_hat = contact.d_hat 0.005 um give 1.676e4. A VALUE computed at authoring time (PI 2026-09-29 decision 12: kept valued). Re-compute when contact.d_hat or F_hold changes. Numerical, not in KB source_audit

contact.sdf.eta

the SDF line-search fraction (SdfParams.eta in (0, 1)): in one line search a node-face pair may close at most eta of its gap at the line search's START (the swept-CCD floor is (1 - eta) gap(0), so 0.9 leaves 10 %), however many advances the bound takes (C3 39c6161b8). The same fraction as contact.barrier.safety, so both contact terms leave the same share of a gap per line search. Method source: additive CCD (Li, Kaufman, Jiang 2021, Codimensional Incremental Potential Contact, ACM TOG 40(4)) — NOT in the KB (no row names it, checked 2026-09-24); registration goes through the KB procedure, not this file

strand-contact-1009 (Lead/PI AUTO-1009-ALL 2026-10-10, decision 2): 1 = the build's strand-strand clearance pass (cell/build/clearance.clear_strand_pairs) moves every non-exempt pair of strand capsules out of xi before the world is made, and the crosslinker centres clear of strands and each other before their arms are drawn. F9-1013: the pass now ends with 0 strand pairs inside xi and the surface check passing on C02, P05 AND U1 (host), but the row stays 0: on a whole-cell build it pushes the DECLARED bundles apart too (their filament spacing lies inside the xi + d_hat it clears to: the coarse cell's filopodium then occupies no bundle relation), and two placements after it put pairs back inside xi (bound NMII heads; crosslinker centres drawn near the filaments) — see ALL_ON.toml

engine.example.toml · range

contact.strand_clearance.release_gap_rel

assemble.build_tables / clearance.clear_strand_pairs (F9-1013): a strand pair closer than xi + this x contact.d_hat after a cycle is CLOSE — the build runs another cycle, and that cycle's release pass pushes exactly the close pairs out to xi + d_hat. 0 = only the pairs inside xi (the start guard's count). Above 0 because a pair a hair outside xi is no start either: the log barrier's force is kappa (2 x ln(e/d_hat) + x^2/e), x = e - d_hat, i.e. 1.19 kappa d_hat at e = d_hat/2 and growing as 1/e below (12 kappa d_hat at d_hat/10; the first U1 build that reached 0 inside xi left one pair at e < 5e-4 nm). 0.5 = the lower half of the band, a convention, not fitted to a count; SWEPT-able: 1.0 releases every in-band pair (and gives up keeping their chords)

contact.strand_clearance.max_cycles

assemble.build_tables (F9-1013; was the literal 2): cycles of (strand pass, whole surface pass, census) before the build goes on with what is left; cycle 0 keeps every chord and junction distance, later cycles release the close pairs (release_gap_rel); a cycle is the last once no pair is close after the surface pass. C02, P05 host builds end in cycle 0, U1 in cycle 1; what is left after the cap is REPORTED (STRAND_REPORT overlap_after_surfaces) and the universal launches' start census then records it or refuses (CoreOptions.start_overlaps)

engine.example.toml · range

engine411–100numerical
contact.universal.bond_exempt_band

MOTOR2-1014 (2026-10-14): the universal contact's BOND exemption rule (energy/barrier.py _exempt, universal_pairs_np), a declared arm. 0 = today: a node pair joined by a live relation is exempt only when the relation's rest is below the pair's xi. 1 = below xi + contact.d_hat, the bound the contour rule already uses: a relation resting inside the barrier's activation band can never sit at its rest while the pair is listed (the barrier is active there and +inf at xi), so contact holds it in tension at every step. Found by the MOTOR-1014 stroke twin: the crossbridge rests at r_md + r_actin = xi by derivation and the barrier pushes it to ~11.7 nm (d - xi ~ 0.9 d_hat). Excluding bonded 1-2 pairs from the non-bonded excluded volume is the molecular-dynamics convention. With 1, a bound tip's distance from its own actin segment is the relation's and the head's angle laws' (law 6, nmii.md_actin_radial_k_theta, holds it radial; without law 6 the tip pivots about its site at zero energy), every OTHER actin segment stays a pair. A rule, not a fitted number

CoreOptions.prerelax_qs_growth (W8-PRE-1015, read only by prerelax_solve = quasi_static): the factor by which each start-relaxation pass's pseudo-time tau_k grows (tau_k = tau_0 growth^k up to prerelax_qs_dt_max_ratio x tau_0). Every x_k-anchored dissipation of the pass's Pi (node drag, Stokes face friction, surface viscosity rows, the permeation's V(x_k)) is ~ 1/tau, so the growth is the rate at which Pi_k -> E and the pass-boundary exposure of grad E falls. No derivable value: SWEPT. Device record b25_u1conv_c8b42ec1c u1pcjc (constant tau 1e-3 s): Pi at the start of pass 1 was 4.975 pN um below Pi at the end of pass 0 (3.2 % of that pass's descent), the start force 0.99 pN after an end force of 0.033 pN

core.prerelax_qs_dt_max_ratio

CoreOptions.prerelax_qs_cap (W8-PRE-1015, read only by prerelax_solve = quasi_static): the largest pass time as a multiple of the first pass's tau_0 (the run's dt, or prerelax_dt). The node drag D = 6 pi eta R / tau is the only regulariser of E's soft and translational modes in the pass; D = 0.055 pN/um at tau 1e-3 s, so the cap bounds how far it is allowed to fall (cap 100: D = 5.5e-4). Too large a cap risks a singular H + D (a stalled or unreached pass, recorded as such); too small leaves the exposure. No derivable value: SWEPT, swept per case (CoreOptions field), never edited inline after a run

BENDREST-ROUND-1015 (cell build arm build.bend_rest_snap): the factor k of the roundoff bound k x eps64 x (|x_i| + 2|x_j| + |x_k|) under which an as-built bending rest |x_i - 2x_j + x_k| is the straight rest (assemble.roundoff_rest_rows). Derived, not tuned: collinear points whose coordinates were each stored after m correctly rounded operations (|dx| <= m u |x|, u = eps64 / 2) give a second difference, evaluated in 2 more roundings (2 x_j is exact), of at most (m + 2) u (|x_i| + 2|x_j| + |x_k|) per component (and in the 2-norm, by the triangle inequality); k = (m + 2) / 2 = 2 for m = 2, the builders' x = c + s u (one multiply, one add per coordinate). Host builds 2026-10-15 (7452ab26b): every positive roundoff rest measured at ratio <= 0.36 (C02 / U1 NMII, P08 arm 1 MT), every genuinely bent as-built rest at >= 8.8e10 - any k in the range classifies the measured worlds identically. M = 1 is the monotone Armijo test bit for bit. 10 is the window customary since GLL 1986, set before any result of this lane; a solver convention with no derivation, so SWEPT over [1, 20]. engine.example.toml · range

engine0.110.0–1.0numerical
newton.tol_thermal_eps

newton.TOL_EPS, tol_rule = thermal_displacement (PI 2026-10-09 14:17 TOLF-REDERIVE, 14:39 clarification: a DEFINITION of converged, not a tighter tolerance; transcript ef9e7f17). Definition: a step is converged when, at every node, the displacement its remaining force would cause (|g_i|/D_i, the D-bound of A^-1 g since A >= D) is at most eps times the displacement the same step's thermal noise causes (sigma_i = sqrt(2 kT gamma_i/dt)/D_i, the anchor shift thermal._kick_one draws). Value argued from the definition, not from outcomes: an error of eps sigma changes the per-step displacement variance by <= eps^2 if uncorrelated with the kick (<= 2 eps + eps^2 if fully correlated, a bias); eps = 0.1 -> 1 %, which a variance (MSD, fluctuation spectrum) estimated from N independent samples resolves only for N >~ 2/eps^4 = 2e4 (relative SE sqrt(2/N)) — below the resolution of the ensembles this engine reports per step. Not chosen to pass or to tighten: on the U1/MINI builds kT/dx corresponds to eps_i = sigma_i,free/(2 dx) = 1.28 (actin, dt 1e-4), 4.05 (dt 1e-3), 12.8 (dt 1e-2) (dev/experiments/tol_rule_study --map); the declared convergence study (PENDING_DEFAULT_FLIPS tol-rule-intrinsic) tests the definition's claim. CORRECTED 2026-10-09 (Codex review NN-2026-10-09-convergence-definition-review; PI 15:20 AUTO-1009-ALL): |g_i|/s_i <= eps is a BACKWARD-ERROR statement (the end iterate solves the step exactly under an extra nodal force of at most eps x the kick scale); |g_i|/D_i is NOT a per-node bound on the displacement error (A >= D bounds the whole D-norm only) and the variance figures above are conditional scale arguments (uncorrelated residual and kick are not shown). eps = 0.1 is the arm under verification; also the thermal fraction of tol_rule = intrinsic

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.110.001–1.0numerical
newton.tol_athermal_eps_dx

newton.TOL_EPS_DX, tol_rule = thermal_displacement on a node with NO thermal scale (kT = 0, R = 0, dormant). Definition without noise: there is no displacement the step makes indistinguishable, so the reference becomes the resolution of the discretisation itself — a step is converged when the displacement its remaining force would cause is at most this fraction of the grid spacing dx (resolution.spacing), i.e. below what the node/grid representation can resolve. 0.1 = the stage-1 contract's tol_x = 0.1 dx (3 A1; score_converged_step tol_x_um). PROPOSAL flagged for PI review: it is per step, so N steps can accumulate up to N x this as drift; an observable-referenced T = 0 tolerance is the alternative

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.110.001–1.0numerical
newton.tol_lte_theta

newton.TOL_THETA, tol_rule = intrinsic (PI 2026-10-09 15:20 AUTO-1009-ALL, transcript ef9e7f17; DESIGN-2026-10-09-convergence-definition): the solver's remaining backward error on a node is held to theta x the step's own backward-Euler local truncation error expressed as a force, tau_i = |grad E_i(x) - grad E_i(x0)|/2 (the BE-minus-trapezoid difference of the step, the BDF1 Milne-device estimate). Convention source: the implicit-integrator practice of solving the corrector to a fixed fraction of the local-error budget (SUNDIALS CVODE nonlinear convergence coefficient nlscoef, default 0.1; Hindmarsh et al. 2005 ACM TOMS 31:363 and the CVODE user guide; SECONDARY, quote to be verified through the KB route before citing in a deliverable) — the same 0.1 as newton.tol_thermal_eps, so the T > 0 and T = 0 branches hold the same fraction of their intrinsic scale. Not chosen to pass: an arm under verification (U1 round 7, tol_rule_study)

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.110.01–1.0numerical
newton.tol_lte_atol_dx

newton.TOL_LTE_ATOL_DX, tol_rule = intrinsic: the absolute floor of the LTE scale in units of dx (resolution.spacing), the CVODE atol role — a step whose estimated truncation error is below this length (a stationary or very slow node) is held to theta x this length, never to zero (an unreachable stop). 0.1 = the stage-1 contract's tol_x = 0.1 dx (3 A1; score_converged_step tol_x_um), so the T = 0 floor is theta x tol_x = 0.01 dx. PI decision item (DESIGN-2026-10-09-convergence-definition 7): the absolute state budget of a T = 0 world is a declaration, not derivable from the step

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.110.001–1.0numerical
newton.tol_lte_cap_dx

newton.TOL_LTE_CAP_DX, tol_rule = intrinsic: the geometric guard — the LTE scale is capped at this many dx (resolution.spacing). An estimate beyond one grid spacing is outside the smooth-BE estimator's validity (a contact activation, a kinetic jump, a stiff mode's O(1) BE error) and may not loosen the stop further; at theta 0.1 the cap's budget is 0.1 dx, the thermal_displacement arm's T = 0 branch (newton.tol_athermal_eps_dx). dx is a guard here, never the reference (Codex review NN-2026-10-09 4)

SPEED-1015 (amg_device.bottom_factor): the column-block width of the dense bottom's Cholesky under CoreOptions.coarse_bottom_blocked (the declared arm; off = one column per launch). Every lower entry takes the same operations in the same order either way (the same factor bits), so the row trades launches (3 N / width) and the trailing update's memory traffic (once per block, not per column) against the single-thread diagonal block (width^3 / 6 serial FMA per block). growth.tip_tail.k_cap

ring capacity K of a monomer-resolved end (aleph/physics/tip_tail.py): owned sub-node slots behind the tip. Must be >= n_c + k_min (n_c = round(resolution.spacing / unit length), 19 for actin at 50 nm / 2.7 nm) or the build refuses. A resolution choice, not a cell parameter; each tail carves k_cap + body_pool dormant nodes from its family's pool

engine.example.toml · range

engine24121–64example
growth.tip_tail.k_min

units kept in the tail after a coarsen (k_min >= 1; the joint at the tip's root needs the odd segment plus one δ row): a coarsen fires at m >= n_c + k_min, so a refine (at m = 0) never follows one. Numerical hysteresis, not physics

engine.example.toml · range

engine311–8example
growth.tip_tail.body_pool

body nodes (with one segment row and one triple row each) a tail holds for its coarsens: each coarsen pops one, each refine of a tail-made body row pushes one back; an empty pool refuses the coarsen and counts it (pool_exhausted) — the tail then holds k_cap units and refuses further splits (refuse_full). Sizing, not physics: at 116 /s a 51 nm coarsen every ~0.16 s, so 4 covers ~0.7 s of net growth per end

engine.example.toml · range

engine411–64example
growth.tip_tail.adapt_distance

T_adapt (PI D3, the default T arm): an end gets a tail at build iff its tip lies within this distance of a surface node (the obstacle the ratchet pushes); farther ends keep the coarse displacement stroke (C1). A selection radius, not physics; 0.1 um = 2 x resolution.spacing. Build-time selection only — an end that later approaches an obstacle stays coarse (dynamic refinement is not built)

engine.example.toml · range

engine0.1um0.0–10.0example
growth.leap_cap

CoreOptions.growth_leap's undeclared value (L2-turn-on-1013; the LEAP arm, PI AUTO-1010-NIGHT, 41238db75; the ALL-ON profile's cap): strokes per (slot, direction) per step on the accumulated clock. A bound on the step's work, not a rate: it binds only when r*dt exceeds it (the clock then drains at this many per step and the excess is counted in 'deferred'); below that every crossed threshold fires and the step is identical to cap 1 at r*dt < 1. Cut to what the stroke band allows (cap*delta <= l_max - l_min) per world, recorded. No measurement brackets it: the number is a ceiling on one step's events (SWEEP: 1 = the incumbent one-fire cap)

cloud->particle exchange: the substep keeps the particle step s = sqrt(2 D dt) <= emit_reach x h, because emission considers the 26 neighbours only. A method choice, not physics

engine.example.toml · range

ssa.diffusion_split_max_p

finite_reactions.CompartmentSSA: the largest TOTAL jump probability one molecule takes in one diffusion substep, 2 DIM D dt_sub / h^2 (each face 1/6 of it); the step is split into ceil(2 DIM D_max dt / h^2 / this) substeps. A method choice of the operator split, not physics: one substep is exact for the independent-walker marginal at any value <= 1/2 (each molecule one uniform, six disjoint direction slots), the bound only keeps the Lie-split reaction-diffusion error small (O(dt_sub)); 0.25 keeps >= 75 % of the molecules in place per substep. Swept by the host mode-decay test (decay law e^{-lambda_k t} vs substep size)

rigid.sagitta_frac

L4a-RIGID-1015 (energy/rigidbody.RigidBodies.limit): the rotation cap's largest departure of a body node's rigid line-search path from the straight line the contact CCD certified, as a fraction of contact.d_hat; the cap lowers alpha_max so rho_b (alpha |omega|)^2 / 2 <= this x d_hat (rho_b the body's largest node distance from its centroid; the remainder bound |e^(i theta) - 1 - i theta| <= theta^2 / 2). A safety fraction of the method, not physics: it sets how far one line search may rotate a body near contact, never Pi, its minimiser or the stop. 0.1 = one tenth of the barrier's activation band, the same order as the CCD's own kept share (1 - contact.barrier.safety); not fitted. Build refuses 2 x this x d_hat >= the smallest body exclusion radius

SimuCell3D local_mesh_refiner.hpp:45-48 splits at lmax = 3 lmin; with l_min_ratio 0.5 this keeps that ratio 3 (and l_max >= 2 l_min, so a split's halves are not collapse candidates — surface_remesh.RemeshParams refuses below). steps between two remesh events (an event runs after step k when (k + 1) % every == 0, between solves). SimuCell3D checks its topology events every 5 steps (solver.cpp:121). Cadence of a declared topology event, not a step judgement (directive 7)

surface.remesh.reserve

dormant nodes reserved at build for the remesh splits, as a fraction of the face-node count (face slots F + 2 x that; surface_remesh.reserve_tables; world.remesh_pool). Read ONLY by a build that declares a remeshed surface (a scene surface's remesh = true; the cell declaration's SurfaceProps.remesh, none today): every other build is unchanged. 1.0 lets the face-node count double before the reserve runs out. Sizing, not physics: an exhausted reserve stops the splits and is counted (pool_short / capacity_short), never silent

cortex.proximal_fraction

the fraction of cortex filaments laid in the membrane-proximal HALF of the shell (build/cortex._depth; 0.5 = uniform through the thickness, the pre-2026-09-17 build). The cortex is densest under the membrane (Clark 2013 Biophys J 105:570 — cortical actin within ~100-200 nm of the membrane, thickness profile from super-resolution; Chugh 2017 Nat Cell Biol 19:689 — thickness/density set by the length distribution): a value above 0.5 puts that structure in. RESULT-2026-09-15 s10.15: at 0.5, 9.1 % of membrane vertices are farther than erm.reach (45 nm) from any cortex segment at build. Not sourced as a number; SET 0.8 on 2026-09-17 11:15 from the build measurement (RESULT-2026-09-15 s10.16, NMII minifilaments on the same profile): membrane vertices beyond erm.reach 9.1 % (0.5) -> 2.4 % (0.8), NMII heads beyond crossbridge.reach 14.4 % -> 12.8 %; 0.9 was not taken (the profile then has 90 % of the cortex in 100 nm, beyond what the density literature supports).

cortex.thickness

measured thickness not trusted (PI 2026-10-07). SWEPT (SWEEP-ALL-UNCERTAIN, PI 20:06) over a range wider than every measurement, so the comparison arm sweeps it rather than holding a measured point. COMPARISON ARM ONLY (cortex.build_arm = 0, the fixed shell): PI A9 2026-10-07 20:16 KST (transcript ef9e7f17) — the cortex thickness EMERGES from length distributions and self-assembly, and measured thicknesses are neither inputs nor targets. Arms 1 and 2 (build/cortex_emergent) do not read this row; their thickness is the observable cortex_emergence.PRIMARY. Value kept as the incumbent shell's (was SOURCED: h_cortex ~200 nm — Salbreux 2012 TCB, Charras 2008 BJ, Clark 2013 BJ, KB-3.1 / KB-3.5). Still read by cortex_shell for NMII / IF / MT / microvillus / cytoplasm-actin placement and the nucleator pool volume in every arm (DESIGN-2026-10-07-emergent-cortex §6, open)

cortex.formin_mass_fraction

formin share of the cortical actin protomers in filaments — Fritzsche 2016 Sci Adv (KB Fritzsche2016_SciAdv, audit OK) p0: "less than 10% of the filaments, containing 20 to 25% of actin protomers incorporated in filaments, were nucleated by formins"; p3 (the FRAP measurement, their ref 18): "20 to 25% of the total protomers in F-actin"; p7: "they still account for 20 to 25% of the total actin protomers bound in actin filaments". Value = the midpoint (PI 2026-09-25 00:0x); the range is the sweep axis. The build takes the PROTOMER fraction (the measured quantity) and derives the number fraction from it with the two lengths (2.8% of filaments are formin); p0's 'less than 10%' of filaments agrees (2.8%); p7's 'only 10%' does not close with 20-25% and a 10x length under simple averaging — recorded, not resolved. The planned 0.67 (Bovellan 2014) was the Arp2/3 share inverted (Fritzsche p7 cites the knockdowns: Arp2/3 ~30%, Diaph1 ~15% of cortical protomers)

membrane.excess_area

VALUE 0.36 IS A LEUKOCYTE TRANSFER, not an MCF7 measurement (L7, 2026-10-13, literature pass membrane_literature_1013.md): T-lymphocyte SEM 40-49 % / rupture A*/A0 1.22-1.4 (Guillou 2016). The ONLY suspended-MCF7 number is a dielectric folding factor phi = 2.46 +- 0.40, i.e. f = phi - 1 ~ 1.46 (Gascoyne 2013 Electrophoresis, NCI-60 DEP-FFF, Table: MCF7 r 9.08 +- 3.71 um, C_mem 22.2 +- 3.6 mF/m2 over the 9 mF/m2 smooth membrane; full text; the capacitance method sits ~x2 from EM / aspiration on granulocytes, so this is an upper hint, not a point). Neutrophils lyse at 2.1-2.6x area (abstracts). The value is NOT changed here; the range is the literature span and the storage form is the membrane.reservoir_arm axis (sinusoidal wrinkles have no primary source; suspended-cell reservoirs are microvilli, folds, filopodia). EARLIER RANGE 0-0.70 (PI 2026-10-07 20:35 KST, transcript ef9e7f17: the part ladder builds a smooth vesicle, f = 0, and small worlds; the band below stays the physiological one): the CELL's total excess area f = A / A_sphere - 1 (build/membrane: the wrinkle carries f minus the microvillus tubes' measured share). origin E (KB-2026-09-1x-membrane-remainder §3, PI 2026-09-10 23:16; row set (a) = the 09-10 decision table, applied to this file PI 2026-10-06 19:50): f 0.36, band 0.22-0.70 — Guillou 2016 aspiration A*/A0 - 1 on suspended leukocytes 0.22-0.48 (a transfer, stated), SEM stock 0.40-0.49, adherent ceiling 0.7 (Groulx 2006); MCF7/MDA f is KB-GAP. In THIS file microvillus.areal_density = 0, so the isotropic wrinkle (lambda 0.30) carries all of f; the microvillus share 0.18 is the declared variant dev/experiments/ladder/spec_tubes_rows.toml (SPEC=tubes). Was 0.15 [0.06, 0.60] (variant A, endothelial band, PI decision E1) until 2026-10-06

membrane.mu_2d

PI-BATCH-2016 (2026-10-07 20:16 KST, lane cell-structure-1007) A11: a lipid bilayer is a 2D FLUID — zero in-plane shear modulus, finite surface shear viscosity — so the bilayer's own mu_2d is 0; in-plane shear resistance comes from what is attached to it (the spectrin-like skeleton, spectrin.*, tied at face points; the cortex through erm). The old value 10 pN/um is the DECLARED COMPARISON ARM (set this row to 10 and spectrin.enabled to 0). The mesh keeps a declared NUMERICAL regularisation, membrane.mesh_regularisation_mu. Before A11: 2D shear modulus of the surface's in-plane network; every mesh edge is a segment at K_edge = 4 mu_2d / sqrt(3) (rung 5 arm (e): a triangular edge network with axial K has shear modulus sqrt(3) K/4 and area modulus sqrt(3) K/2; PLAN-2026-09-03z §2.3, PLAN-2026-09-03ab §1), rest = as-built. 10 pN/um is the rung-10 rig's EXAMPLE value (rung-10 rig — a development experiment, dev/experiments/ladder/rung10_surface_support.SURFACE_MU_2D since Phase 4 (ffba0ee2)), the one Z1 measured (the surface's dt ceiling 1e-7 -> 1e-6, no inversions) — NOT a bilayer property (a fluid bilayer has no shear modulus; the spectrin/ERM-cortex contribution is the physical carrier and is KB-GAP). Replaces membrane.edge_k: the term is ON for every closed surface and K is DERIVED, never typed (R0' fold, RESULT-2026-09-03-w5-r0prime)

membrane.volume_modulus

PI decision 2026-09-16 18:57: KEEP. The enclosed-volume law p = p0 + K_V (V0 - V)/V0 (Surfaces.k_volume, 2026-09-16, RESULT-2026-09-15 s10.4): the linearised van 't Hoff law of an enclosed ideal solution, K_V = pi_internal = 300 mM x 2577 pN/um^2/mM (a ~300 mOsm internal solution x osmotic.pressure_per_mM; d pi / d ln V = -pi at fixed solute; water crosses on the osmotic time scale, which is far longer than these steps). DERIVED since param-ledger-1013 (PI 2026-10-13 16:30, audit #16): osmotic.external is now a row, so the product is derived instead of typed (300.0 x 2577.0 = 773100.0 exactly, bit-identical to the former typed value; the internal solution is taken isotonic with the medium, as the source above states). It was SWEPT 77310-7731000 (factor 10, 'nothing better'); that range is retired with the typed value: sweep osmotic.external (260-340 mM) or osmotic.pressure_per_mM. An internal osmolarity different from the medium's is a new row, not a number typed here. Since PI 2026-10-07 21:03 (Q5) the K_V/V0 COMPARISON ARM only: with solute.ion_transport = 1 (shipped) the core releases it on every transporting surface and records the replaced value (cell/solute_build.osmotic_term); it acts again only with osmotic.water_permeation = 0.

membrane.inplane_flow_enabled

switch, not a material value: 1 gives every membrane face a lipid COUNT as state and lets that material move between faces along the tension difference (physics.surface_count_flow), so the face-area reference becomes N_f x membrane.lipid_area_per_molecule instead of the area the face was built with (area_constraint_reference = 'count' on the integrate.step path; FaceAreaALM reads Faces.built_area live on the energy core). ON since 2026-10-07 (lane flow-filamin-1007, aleph/docs/v2_audit/NOTE-2026-10-07-inplane-flow.md). The two reasons it shipped 0 are closed: (1) the 'unexplained membrane volume-flux instability (INVENTORY E21/E22)' was RETRACTED the same night by INVENTORY E24 (21:21 KST 2026-09-21) -- a period-2 runaway made by the recorder (engine.sample_block's between-step force pass rewrote surfaces.volume, which the next step's pressure law read), fixed in 4cd5766c0 (sample_block saves and restores what it writes) and verified on a device in INVENTORY E25(d) (EVERY = 1 bounded, -236..+373 um^3/s); it never involved this flow, which came in one minute earlier and was off in every arm; (2) the edge solve now converges by construction (one-unit-of-material stop, warm start, sim.inplane_flow_cg_iters a cap with the residual recorded) instead of a fixed 64 updates at tolerance 0 (record 402: 0.5-1.3 % residual every step). Written, not verified on a device at this value: the live energy core reads the reference only on surfaces listed in [core] face_area. Without it a tether cannot form and, under plate compression, the contact zone and the free zone cannot exchange membrane, so the membrane tension is artificially non-uniform in exactly the experiment that reads cortical tension.

membrane.inplane_friction

PI-GAP, and a STAND-IN that is to be REPLACED rather than sourced. The in-plane flow law v = grad(sigma)/b needs a drag per unit area per unit in-plane velocity; membrane-cortex friction is reported around 1e8-1e9 Pa.s/m (tether-pulling and flow measurements of the Shi/Baumgart kind; 1 Pa.s/m = 1e-6 pN.s/um^3, so 1e2-1e3 in these units) — quoted from memory, NOT read in a paper here and NOT in the KB source_audit, hence EXAMPLE and hence a range that is exploratory and not a confidence interval. The PI's decision (OPTIONS-2026-09-21 item 3) is that this coefficient should EMERGE from the making and breaking of the explicit ERM relations that tie the bilayer to the cortex, the way composite viscosity must be an observable and not an input (directive 9). This row exists so the flow law can run before that emergence is built, and is to be deleted when it is.

envelope.area_modulus

KB-2026-09-06-nuclear-envelope-shear-modulus §2: unbound from membrane.area_modulus — the nuclear envelope is TWO bilayers in parallel, so K_A = 2 x the single-bilayer value. Rawicz 2000 Biophys J 79:328 (10.1016/S0006-3495(00)76295-3, SE211, audit OK; KB-3.B1.3 verified/High) K_A = 243 mN/m +/- 10 % across 12 PCs = 2.43e5 pN/um -> 4.86e5 here. This is the GLOBAL area term (assemble.py k_area -> Surfaces.k_area, g = k_area/area0 * dA), additive to the mu_2d edge network's own areal response K_A = 2 mu_2d; the membranes are slack until envelope.excess_area = 0.30 is spent, which is why the lamina (Dahl 25 mN/m) and not the bilayers sets the measured NE stiffness. The lamina's own contribution is envelope.mu_2d + the lamina population, NOT this row. 10.1016/S0006-3495(00)76295-3

spec.example.toml · range

cell486000.0pN/um162000.0–1458000.0sweptmodel computed
envelope.mu_2d

KB-2026-09-06-nuclear-envelope-shear-modulus §1: unbound from membrane.mu_2d — the plasma membrane's mu is carried by the spectrin/ERM-cortex, the NE's by the NPC-lamin connections; not the same quantity. NO source isolates the double-bilayer + NPC in-plane shear from the lamina's, because the lamin meshwork is its own population here (build/lamina.py). What the OK-verdict evidence constrains is the SUM envelope+lamina: Stephens 2017 MBoC 28:1984 (10.1091/mbc.E16-09-0653, audit OK) single-nucleus micromanipulation gives a short-extension stiffness 0.41-0.70 nN/um with 1.5-2.5x strain stiffening carried by lamin-A/C, i.e. a lamin-attributable 2.5e2-7.5e2 pN/um for a somatic mammalian nucleus (a shell stiffness k ~ C*mu, C = O(1) — order of magnitude, not a modulus). The lamina as BUILT already delivers 1.3e2-5.1e2 pN/um (EA = material.if.E * pi * material.if.radius^2 = 471 pN over lamina.filament = 0.4 um -> k_edge 1178 pN/um; mu = sqrt(3)k/4 = 510 affine, 128 after the z=4.5 vs z_c=4 knockdown), so 2.5e2 here puts the sum at 3.8e2-7.6e2 pN/um, inside the measured band. Ceiling 2.5e4 = Dahl 2004 J Cell Sci 117:4779 (10.1242/jcs.01357, audit OK, SE562): 25 mN/m network elastic modulus, micropipette aspiration of ISOLATED XENOPUS OOCYTE envelopes — an amphibian lamin-B-rich oocyte NE, 30-100x above the somatic band, and Swift 2013 (10.1126/science.1240104, audit OK) is why it may not be transferred to a human somatic cell unqualified. Dahl does not split K_A from mu; the engine's triangular network fixes K_A = 2 mu, and the measured K/mu is 1.5 +/- 0.3 (HeLa, Rowat 2005) to 5.1 +/- 1.3 (WT MEF, Rowat 2006) — both PENDING SE registration, see the KB doc §3. Its own K_edge = 4 mu_2d / sqrt(3) = 577 pN/um per envelope edge (PLAN-2026-09-03ab §1), x25 tonight's 23.094: the envelope's in-plane branch moves 1.9e5 -> 4.7e6 /s (object_spectra_20260905T152006Z), still below the IF/MT branches. The gate is NOT this row: aspirate the built nucleus and score k_short / k_long against Stephens 0.41-0.70 nN/um and 1.5-2.5x. 10.1091/mbc.E16-09-0653

axial spacing of consecutive crowns: the myosin II rod's parallel stagger, Kaufmann & Schwarz 2020 PLoS Comput Biol 16:e1007801 (SE553 OK): 'Electron microscopy and scattering experiments of myosin II and myosin II rod-fragments revealed prominent axial staggers of 14.3 nm, 43.2 nm and (less frequently observed) 72 nm between adjacent parallel myosin rods'. Billington 2013 (SE426 OK) counts molecules assuming 'a head spacing of 14.3 nm along the filament'; Niederman 1975 (SE584 OK) gives '14-15 nm intervals' for platelet myosin. Borrowed from myosin II generally for the NMII crown: EXAMPLE. Decision 31

nmii.s2_length

M-D2-GEOM / M-GEOM-2 / M-LFREE (PI 2026-10-06 21:52 KST; lane motor-rig-1006): the S2 = the FREE part of the myosin rod, peeled off the backbone bundle at its anchor site (the rest of nmii.rod_length is the bound part, inside the bundle). No NM2 measurement of the free length (GAP). SWEPT band, both ends computed at authoring from the other rows (re-compute if any changes): UPPER 0.0823391 = aleph/cell/derive.s2_free_length_max at the reach band's LOW end (0.00885): the longest free rod whose peel point does not cross the centre given the heads on the measured bare zone; the bound rises with the reach (0.0863 at the EXAMPLE reach, 0.0942 at 0.050), so the low end's is the one every reach in the band admits (nmii.s2_length_max is the current reach's, and build/nmii refuses a crossing). LOWER 0.0403694 (rounded UP from 0.04036932) = the shortest rod that can carry the head to the reach band's HIGH end, 0.050 - (lever_arm + motor_domain_length / 2) cos(head_splay) (a perpendicular rod): geometry, not a measurement. Kaufmann & Schwarz 2020 (SE553 OK), a MODEL, proxy only: 'the free part of the rod would be of length 85–135 nm (using a rod length of 160 nm)' — its whole band lies ABOVE the no-crossing bound here (reported, PI M-LFREE). EXAMPLE 0.0613542 = the band's midpoint, chosen for no outcome. Cut into ceil(length / nmii.arm_seg) equal pieces (nmii.s2_seg, directive 6).

nmii.s2_perp_distance

M-D2-GEOM / M-BBR (PI 2026-10-06 21:52 KST; lane motor-rig-1006): the HEAD's perpendicular reach from the backbone axis — the motor-domain centre, measured in the S2's own radial plane (aleph/cell/derive.s2_departure_angle) — the DECLARED quantity from which the S2 departure angle is derived. Measured bound: Niederman & Pollard 1975 J Cell Biol 67:72 (SE584 OK), platelet NM2A, negative stain: the heads 'swing out up to 50 nm from the shaft of the filament' (a qualitative maximum, no n). Measured state distribution: Billington et al. 2013 J Biol Chem 288:33398 (SE426 OK): 70 / 88 / 73 % of NM2A / B / C filaments are COMPACT ('the heads are packed closely against the backbone'), and the splayed 'bouquet' increases with RLC phosphorylation. Model only: Kaufmann & Schwarz 2020 PLoS Comput Biol 16:e1007801 (SE553 OK) — a MODEL, proxy only: heads 40–90 nm off the backbone (its upper half exceeds the only measured maximum). No NM2 measurement of the reach distribution (GAP). SWEPT band: low = the COMPACT state, the head against the backbone = nmii.backbone_radius + nmii.motor_domain_radius = 0.0056 + 0.00325 (computed at authoring after M-BBR; re-compute if either changes); high = Niederman's measured maximum 0.050. EXAMPLE 0.029425 = the band's midpoint: a placeholder chosen for no outcome; the in-vitro majority is compact (Billington), splay grows with RLC phosphorylation — the PI's M-D2 choice.

L2-turn-on-1013 (PI 2026-10-13 'the solved fix is the default'): the DEFAULT is 1. Device evidence of the pole at form 0: NIGHT-4090-110/115 MINI M1/M2 (01_DECISIONS 2026-10-09/10 rows): LeverTerm spikes 1.8e4 / 1.8e5 pN; NIGHT-4090-116 (same world, form 1): 'no LeverTerm spike - slew form 1 removed it'; U1_FLOOR_LOCALIZE_1009: 1.53e4 pN froze the U1 ratchet seed-3 solve. WHY: the crossbridge relation is a scalar bond (rest r_md + r_actin), so the tip PIVOTS about its site point at zero energy and laws 2-4 all refer to the actin tangent, not to the site — the host twin (dev/experiments/ladder/stroke_twin.py, one head on one trapped actin segment, T = 0 statics) puts 5.500 of the 5.5-nm stroke into that pivot (tip offset 81 -> 127 deg to tau, toward the axis), filament 0.000 nm, trap force 0. Steric exclusion alone does not close it (a tip sliding along tau on the actin's cylinder keeps its distance to the axis: the bond stretch is second order). The bound actomyosin interface is stereospecific; no measured angular stiffness of the tip about its site exists (GAP). ARM value (not shipped): 0.0368 = crossbridge.k x crossbridge.rest_len^2 = 700 x 0.00725^2, the convention of nmii.md_actin_k_theta / lever_k_theta (the measured crossbridge stiffness at the joint's own arm); twin at the arm: filament 1.39 of 5.5 nm into a 2 x 50 pN/um trap. DEVICE: built (MOTOR2-1014) — lever_table hands a value > 0 to LeverTable(k6) as element q = 4 (law code 6) of each head group; 0 keeps the four-element table of today. | independent of the four sibling joint laws.

nmii.joint_stiffness_rule

switch, not a measurement (MOTOR2-1014, PI MOTOR-SERIES-DERIVE 2026-10-14 23:0x, 01_DECISIONS): how the bound head's stroke-path joint stiffnesses are set. 0 = each row as written (each joint alone at crossbridge.k x its arm^2: the head's series compliance is then the SUM of their compliances, ~N / crossbridge.k) — today, kept as the parallel arm; 1 = build/nmii multiplies laws 2, 3 and 6 (nmii.md_actin_k_theta, nmii.lever_k_theta, nmii.md_actin_radial_k_theta) by nmii.head_series_scale so their series compliance is the measured 1 / crossbridge.k; 2 (MYOSERIES-1015, candidate (a), a parallel arm of 1) = the same rule on the GEOMETRIC moment arms of the built head, |u x tau| of each law's own vector at its bound rest (law 2 |m - c| sin nmii.md_actin_angle, law 3 |fork - c| |sin theta_pre|, law 6 crossbridge.rest_len; derive.head_series_scale_arms in build/nmii, recorded as meta joint_series_arms_um) instead of the rows' lumped lever_arm; scale 3.516 vs rule 1's 2.999 at law 6 = 0.0368. HOST TWIN (stroke_twin.py --myoseries, stroke_twin_myoseries_1015.json, T = 0 statics; not device evidence): head alone 704 pN/um (rule 1: 500), with the S2 in series 44.1 (rule 1: 43.6) — the head-alone reads come from a state-1 reference minimum that stalls at 1.5e-5..4.5e-5 pN on the S2 azimuth zero mode; with nmii.s2_crown_backbone_k_theta at its arm (converged, 1e-11 pN) the head alone reads 565 (rule 2) / 483 (rule 1). Read by build/nmii (absent = 0).

nmii.s2_crown_pair_angle

MOTOR2-1014 (PI MOTOR-S2-CROWN, 2026-10-14 23:0x): the rest of the S2 crown law (nmii.s2_crown_k_theta) — the angle two S2 roots of one crown subtend at their shared anchor site, DERIVED acos(cos^2 theta + sin^2 theta cos(2 pi / M)) (aleph/cell/derive.crown_pair_angle) from nmii.s2_rest_angle and nmii.molecules_per_crown: build/nmii's crown rule (consecutive molecules 2 pi / M apart in azimuth), a DECLARED clearance rule, not biology (no NMII crown order is known). build/nmii checks the built angle against it.

spec.example.toml · derived

cellderived (crown_pair_angle)radexample
nmii.s2_crown_k_theta

the S2 CROWN law (MOTOR2-1014, PI MOTOR-S2-CROWN 2026-10-14 23:0x, 01_DECISIONS): E = 1/2 k (gamma - gamma0)^2, gamma = the angle the first rod nodes of two neighbouring molecules of one crown subtend at their shared anchor site (energy.siteangle law 2, LAW_PAIR; a node relation, directive 2), rest nmii.s2_crown_pair_angle; build/nmii emits one per neighbour pair of a crown (a ring for M >= 3; refused at M = 2, where the pair angle is stationary in the azimuth). WHY: the root law (nmii.s2_root_k_theta, pairangle.site_angle) holds only the root's angle to the backbone axis, a cone: the S2's azimuth about the axis is a zero mode, and the MOTOR-1014 stroke twin puts the whole 5.5-nm stroke into it when the actin is tilted 30/60 deg. The law ties a root's azimuth to its crown neighbours; the crown's common roll about the backbone axis remains (a rigid roll of the crown, resisted by its other bound heads and the fluid; no inter-crown or backbone-frame law here). GAP — no measured azimuthal stiffness of an S2 at the thick filament surface. ARM value (not shipped): 0.0948 = nmii.s2_root_k_theta x sin^2(gamma0) / (2 sin^2(theta) sin^2(2 pi / M)) at the example rows — the root's own clamped-rod bending (an isotropic root: the same stiffness against an azimuthal swing sin(theta) dpsi of the first piece as against a polar one), converted to the pair angle of a molecule in two ring pairs. | independent of nmii.s2_root_k_theta (a different joint law; same rod scale, unsourced).

spec.example.toml · range

cell0.0pN*um/rad^20.0–0.948swept
nmii.s2_crown_backbone_k_theta

the BACKBONE-FRAME crown law (MYOSERIES-1015, Lead brief 2026-10-15: candidate (b) of the 43.6 vs ~700 pN/um series stiffness, PARALLEL-TRACKS arm beside the crown ring nmii.s2_crown_k_theta): E = 1/2 k (gamma - gamma0)^2, gamma = the angle the first rod nodes of two molecules subtend at the inner one's anchor site (energy.siteangle law 2, LAW_PAIR, the crown ring's element; a node relation, directive 2) for each molecule m of crown k and molecule m of crown k + 1 of the same half, and across the bare zone half 0 crown 0 m to half 1 crown 1 m (each pair pi / M apart in azimuth, build/nmii's crown rule); rest = the BUILT angle (geometry, recorded per element). WHY: the backbone is a colinear bead chain with no twist frame; the crown ring ties a root to its crown neighbours but leaves the crown's common roll free (the stroke twin: S2 takes the 5.5 nm at 30/60 deg with the crown roots free). Referencing each crown to the next along the backbone closes every internal roll; the object's rigid roll remains (rotation invariance). Emitted by build/nmii when > 0; refused at molecules_per_crown < 2 or crowns_per_end < 2. GAP — no measured azimuthal stiffness of an S2 at the thick filament surface. ARM value (not shipped; the twin and the case lines): 0.0580 = nmii.s2_root_k_theta x sin^2(theta) / (2 (dgamma/dpsi)^2) at the example rows, dgamma/dpsi = 0.28393 rad/rad (the along-backbone pair's angle per azimuth of its inner root, the built element differentiated at authoring) — the crown law's isotropic-root conversion (an azimuthal swing sin(theta) dpsi of the first piece costs what a polar one does) for an interior root in two pairs; the across-bare-zone pair is softer (dgamma/dpsi 0.098) at the same k. HOST TWIN (stroke_twin.py --myoseries, the next crown's roots held as the backbone frame; T = 0 statics, not device evidence): series stiffness with the S2 in series 43.6 -> 65.7 pN/um (rule 1), 44.1 -> 66.6 (rule 2); the state-1 minimum converges (1e-11 pN, was stalled at 4.5e-5 on the azimuth zero mode). Still below crossbridge.k's band (100-4600): the S2's own bending stays in series. | independent of nmii.s2_crown_k_theta and nmii.s2_root_k_theta (different joint laws; same rod scale, unsourced).

nmii.lever_k_theta

law 3's angular stiffness = the explicit lever, option (e) (angle between fork - c and the bound site's barbed-end actin tangent, vertex c; bound only; DESIGN-2026-10-04-nmii-two-node-head; PI 2026-10-04 19:11 M-D3/M-D1 (transcript ceef984b); candidate evidence aleph/outputs/tag_kb/SE_REGISTRATION_CANDIDATES_2026-10-04_nmii-head-geometry.md (SourceEvidence not yet registered by the PI)). Its rests are NOT rows: theta_pre = pi/2 + Delta/2 before the stroke and theta_post = pi/2 - Delta/2 after it, Delta = nmii_molecules.lever_swing = 2 asin(crossbridge.stroke / (2 nmii.lever_arm)). The symmetry about pi/2 is a declared CONVENTION (it makes the fork's axial step exactly the chord = crossbridge.stroke for every lever azimuth): no absolute pre-stroke lever angle to actin is known for any myosin II (GAP, design §5). GAP — no source: no measured angular stiffness of this joint (the KB has none; design §4 Q2). EXAMPLE build value at the torque scale of the measured crossbridge stiffness carried by the lever, crossbridge.k x nmii.lever_arm^2 = 700 pN/um x (0.0075 um)^2 = 0.0394 pN.um/rad^2 (thermal sigma ~ sqrt(kT/k) = 19 deg at 310 K); a scale, not a measurement. Range: f_stall x lever_arm at crossbridge.f_stall's band low (0.5 pN x 0.0075 um = 0.00375) to crossbridge.k's band high x lever_arm^2 (4600 x 0.0075^2 = 0.259). SWEPT band (lane motor-rig-1006, 2026-10-06: the range above is the axis the PI sweeps, in pN.um/rad^2; reason: no measurement brackets this stiffness, so the band spans the two torque scales the rows can form; the tag stays EXAMPLE until a sweep or a SourceEvidence replaces the value). | independent of nmii.converter_k_theta, nmii.md_actin_k_theta, nmii.md_actin_azimuth_k_theta: four different joint laws; same placeholder value, unsourced.

nmii.converter_angle_free

the converter's internal rest angle (fork, c, m) while the head is FREE (design §4 Q1: a structured joint; DESIGN-2026-10-04-nmii-two-node-head; PI 2026-10-04 19:11 M-D3/M-D1 (transcript ceef984b); candidate evidence aleph/outputs/tag_kb/SE_REGISTRATION_CANDIDATES_2026-10-04_nmii-head-geometry.md (SourceEvidence not yet registered by the PI)). The free head's lever is 'up' with ATP / ADP.Pi: Chinthalapudi & Heissler 2024 (KB ChinthalapudiHeissler2024_CMLS, audit CHECK): 'The closed conformation of the nucleotide binding pocket is linked to the converter and the lever arm in the ‘up’ position (ATP, ADP·P i ) while an open nucleotide binding pocket is associated with the converter and the lever arm in the ‘down’ position (apo, ADP).' No absolute internal angle is known (GAP). DERIVED under the coplanar CONVENTION from laws 2 and 3 (aleph/cell/derive.coplanar_joint_angle): the angle the joint holds when bound pre-stroke with the lever and the motor domain on opposite sides of the actin axis in one plane, md_angle + pi/2 + Delta/2 (wrapped into [0, pi]) = 151.5 deg at the example rows, so a free head binds without a jump in its joint. The 3-state cycle has one free state; the extended cycle's apo/ADP free states (lever 'down') are not distinguished (they hold this same rest)

microtubule.build_arm

which aster build (build-fix-1013, cell/build/microtubule.ARMS; PARALLEL-TRACKS, the arms coexist on one world and one record format): 0 = the steered wrap of 2026-09-14 (unchanged; arms deflected along the SPEC's envelope and the membrane, stopped where they fold), 1 = the smooth build (smooth_arms): MTOC at the cell centre when the world builds no nucleus, minus ends ON the MTOC surface, each arm straight, then one turn of radius microtubule.turn_radius onto the under-membrane limit and its great circle; no arm shortened; 2 = MT-BUILD (PI 2026-10-06 21:25): the same MTOC placement, every arm straight and radial from the MTOC surface, ending at the under-membrane limit (or the envelope's clearance), zero bending at build, the remainder of each arm's slots in the dormant growth pool (the ledger of arm 0's stopped arms); 3 = polymer MASS in, two populations (PI 2026-10-13 15:21, build/microtubule.mass_arms): polymer length = tubulin_total_conc x V_cyt x polymer_fraction / (protofilaments / dimer_rise), lengths drawn from microtubule.length_dist, centrosomal_count straight arms at the MTOC as arm 2 plus free straight rods (minus end uniform by volume, isotropic: EXAMPLE convention, no MCF7 data; Golgi-biased origin and radial bias are unbuilt arms), the MT count DERIVED; meant with microtubule.bend_rest = 1 (PI 15:11). 4 = the smooth wrap (MT-WRAP-1014; PI SWEEP-SIZES-1013 16:14 + MT-BUILD CORRECTION 2026-10-14 21:12, build/microtubule.wrap_arms): MTOC perinuclear when the world builds a nucleus (at the cell centre when it does not), every MT from the MTOC surface, deflected smoothly around the nucleus' offset sphere and turned onto the under-membrane limit and along it (the cortex), curvature <= 1/microtubule.min_bend_radius everywhere, cut where it meets a placed arm (the cut returned to the budget), polymer budget and lengths as arm 3, count derived; meant with microtubule.bend_rest = 1. 5 = arm 4's smooth wrap for the centrosomal MTs + NON-centrosomal (free) MTs on the same path rules (MT-WRAP2-1014, build/microtubule.wrap_free_arms; literature pass 2026-10-14 outputs/lit_mt_1014/REPORT.md: many non-centrosomal MTs), the budget split by microtubule.noncentrosomal_fraction, free minus ends from the Golgi-shell / cytoplasm mix (microtubule.free_origin_golgi_fraction, golgi_shell_inner/outer), bend bound microtubule.min_bend_radius_arm5 (1 kT per dimer, derived), a direction with no turn that fits ending at the limit; meant with microtubule.bend_rest = 1. A switch, not a measurement; 0 until arm 1 is verified on the device (VERIFY-EACH); absent = 0. Default flip = PI decision

microtubule.min_bend_radius

BUILD GEOMETRY of build arm 4 (microtubule.build_arm = 4, MT-WRAP-1014): the smallest radius of curvature a built arm may take (its turn onto the cortex, its deflection off the nucleus); the per-node joint angle is at most 2 asin(seg / 2 min_bend_radius) (5.7 deg at 0.5 um, seg 0.05). 0.5 um = arm 1's microtubule.turn_radius (kept equal so arms 1 and 4 compare like for like), not a measurement: no MCF7 MT curvature distribution is in the KB. With microtubule.bend_rest = 1 the bend carries kappa / (2 rho^2) per um of contour (40 pN um/um at kappa 20 pN um^2, rho 0.5), the energy the solve relaxes. Independent of microtubule.turn_radius (arm 1's): sweeping one does not move the other. PI-GAP — sweep it

spec.example.toml · range

cell0.5um0.25–3.0sweptpi convention
microtubule.min_bend_radius_arm5

BUILD GEOMETRY of build arm 5 (microtubule.build_arm = 5, MT-WRAP2-1014): the smallest radius of curvature a built arm may take. DERIVED from the engine's own rows (typed at 4 digits; tests/product/cell/test_mt_wrap5.py re-derives it and fails if it drifts): the radius at which the bending energy stored per tubulin dimer is 1 kT, R = sqrt(EI / (2 n kT)) with EI = material.microtubule.kappa = 20 pN um^2, n = microtubule.protofilaments / microtubule.dimer_rise = 13 / 0.008 um = 1625 dimers per um, kT = k_B x cell.temperature (310 K) = 4.2800e-3 pN um -> R = sqrt(20 / 13.910) = 1.1991 um (the 2026-10-14 literature report's 1.26 um used EI 22 pN um^2, Gittes 1993). The 1 kT per dimer threshold: Odde et al. 1999 J Cell Sci 112:3283 (abstract, PMID 10504333): 'the rate of microtubule breaking in fibroblast cells increases approximately 40-fold as the elastic energy stored in curved microtubules increases to > approximately 1 kT/tubulin dimer' — not in KB source_audit; the per-dimer convention used here (EI / 2R^2 per um over dimers per um) is ours, Odde's own definition not verified. A build bound, not a measured MCF7 curvature; with microtubule.bend_rest = 1 the built curve is the initial condition the solve relaxes. Independent of microtubule.min_bend_radius (arm 4's, unchanged). PI-GAP — sweep it PMID 10504333

microtubule.noncentrosomal_fraction

build arm 5 (MT-WRAP2-1014, cell/build/microtubule.wrap_free_arms): the share of the polymer budget built as NON-centrosomal (free) MTs — minus ends not on the MTOC (released, broken or Golgi-nucleated: Bartolini & Gundersen 2006 J Cell Sci 119:4155; Efimov et al. 2007 Dev Cell 12:917; Keating et al. 1997 PNAS 94:5078; Waterman-Storer & Salmon 1997 J Cell Biol 139:417 — abstracts read in the 2026-10-14 literature pass, outputs/lit_mt_1014/REPORT.md; not in KB source_audit). A POLYMER (tubulin) fraction: (1 - f) of the budget is built from the MTOC, f as free MTs, each pool closing its own ledger; the built COUNT fraction is reported beside it (meta ledger noncentrosomal_count_fraction_realised), the literature's numbers are counts. No MCF7 number exists: SWEPT; 0.5 = the band's middle, not a measurement

microtubule.dimer_rise

the lattice rise of one tubulin dimer, 8 nm — the end-stroke unit delta of the microtubule family, which is what makes growth_speed a DERIVED on-rate: k_on = growth_speed / (dimer_rise * tubulin_conc) [1/(uM.s)] and the shrink off-rate k_off_b = shrink_speed / dimer_rise [1/s]. LOAD HAZARD, stated where the number is: the on-law multiplies by exp(f*delta/kT), so with delta = 0.008 um and kT = 4.28e-3 pN.um (310 K) one pN of slot load is exp(1.87) = 6.5x and 10 pN is exp(18.7) = 1.3e8 — end_growth clamps the exponent at 50 (f = 26.8 pN), which is a runaway, not a limit. The microtubule family therefore runs under the load the core declares: since 2026-10-07 (growth-load-1007, Lead under the PI autonomy grant, PI ratification pending) growth_load = 'contact' — the obstacle's resisting contact force on the tip along its axis (Peskin-Odell-Oster 1993) — is the live point whenever contact is on, else 'zero'; growth_load = 'stretch' is refused for it in assemble.wire_growth. not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED

DEFAULT 0 -> 1. 0 = legacy: the free pool is the typed row microtubule.tubulin_conc (20 uM, which exceeds microtubule.tubulin_total_conc = 12 uM: free > total) - restore with set microtubule.tubulin_ledger=0. 1 = DEFAULT, conserved = concentration: free = microtubule.tubulin_total_conc x (1 - polymer_fraction) = 12 x 0.32 = 3.84 uM. 2 = conserved = count: free = microtubule.tubulin_total_count x (1 - polymer_fraction) / (N_A x V_cyt), V_cyt the declared cell-minus-nucleus sphere (R 7.5, nc 0.68: 1211.5 um^3), so 5e7 x 0.32 gives 22.0 uM at the default size and follows cell.radius as 1/R^3; build arm 3 then takes its polymer as total_count x polymer_fraction (no volume). growth_speed stays the INPUT: k_on_growing (= growth_speed / (dimer_increment x free / f_w)) is derived and rises 20/3.84 = 5.2-fold under arm 1 (14.22 -> 74.06 /uM/s), 0.9-fold under arm 2. Read through the DERIVED row microtubule.tubulin_free, which every reader of the free pool uses.

erm.areal_density

PI signature 2026-09-11 00:35 (Lead transcript 14373ea7; KB-2026-09-1x-erm-kon-reach §6): the only measured membrane-cortex linker density — Diz-Munoz, Krieg, Bergert, ..., Paluch, Heisenberg 2010 PLoS Biol 8:e1000544 (10.1371/journal.pbio.1000544), dynamic AFM tether spectroscopy on zebrafish mesendoderm progenitors: 41 nm mean lateral spacing = ~600/um^2, strongly reduced by DN-ezrin / ezrin-MO; T_app 46 uN/m, static tether 25-32 pN. At this density the bleb-nucleation threshold of Tinevez 2009 PNAS 106:18581 (10.1073/pnas.0903353106; total tension 200-240 pN/um on a ~1 um cortex hole, suspended L929) is ~18 pN per link = Alert 2015's sigma*/rho_0. Lower edge 100 = the former axis's order; the 2026-08-21 geometric centre 21.2 was 30x below the measurement. MCF7/MDA density KB-GAP. Count is CAPACITY; the build starts the population at occupancy k_on/(k_on+k_off0) (a693ab1f). Harvester candidates, not yet in source_audit 10.1371/journal.pbio.1000544

cell600.01/um^2100.0–600.0swept
erm.k_on

PI signature 2026-09-11 00:35 (Lead transcript 14373ea7; KB-2026-09-1x-erm-kon-reach §2, §6). Sourced as the DATASET pair with erm.k_off0 = 1.3/s (PI decision J): every in-cell observation needs occupancy 0.75-0.9 — Coscoy 2002 PNAS 99:12813 (10.1073/pnas.192084599) two-photon FRAP, 25 % of membrane ezrin exchanging on tau = 5.7 s, rest on 1-2 min; Alert 2015 rho_b*/rho_0 ~ 0.9; Diz-Munoz 2010 density — and with k_off0 1.3 that occupancy is k_on*P ~ 4-12/s (0.88 at 10). Only k_on*P(reach) is identifiable (laws/erm_kinetics). The former '1e4/s (Alert 2015)' is DELETED: Alert's Table 1 takes k_on 1e4 and k_off0 10 from Rognoni 2012 PNAS (10.1073/pnas.1211274109), a FILAMIN Ig20-21 measurement, and fits only chi = k_off/k_on. STATED RESIDUAL: this pair relaxes to occupancy in ~90 ms, while ezrin re-covers a bare bleb membrane in ~5 s (Charras 2006 JCB 175:477, 10.1083/jcb.200602085: ezrin precedes actin by 4.9 +/- 3 s) — a bleb-healing row is ~50x too fast with this pair; the in-cell pair (k_on ~0.2, k_off ~0.03-0.2) needs a re-ratification of k_off0 = a two-row PI decision, OPEN. No mus/ms row sees the difference 10.1073/pnas.192084599

erm.reach

PI signature 2026-09-11 00:35 (Lead transcript 14373ea7; KB-2026-09-1x-erm-kon-reach §3, §6). A pairing filter on the node lattice, not a bond length: the native cortex has 4.59 M nodes in a 0.2 um shell (~0.031 um apart) with its edge at depth 0.018-0.020 um, so a membrane vertex's nearest cortex NODE is at median 0.034 um and the former 0.025 paired 8-11 % of vertices (RESULT-2026-09-10-fixed-build-first-row; Monte-Carlo erm_reach_coverage.json: 0.045 -> 92 %, 0.050 -> 98 %). Inside the molecule: ERM monomer span 10-50 nm, live membrane-cortex boundary gap <10 / <=20 nm (Clausen ... Fritzsche, Eggeling 2017 J Phys D 50:064002, 10.1088/1361-6463/aa52a1, STED on live Jurkat). Every pair RESTS at its built distance (bonds.attach; occupy_at_build a693ab1f) so no initial-load cap is needed — Bell at erm.k 4600 and x_beta 0.7 nm gives k_off(115 pN) ~ 2e8/s, a pair rested at r0 with 25 nm of stretch would die in one step. erm.r0 = 0.020 is the unstressed span. Replaces PI-GAP card E4 10.1088/1361-6463/aa52a1

crosslink.k

PI signature 2026-09-11 17:11 (Lead transcript 14373ea7; KB-2026-09-11-crosslink-bell.md): the effective axial stiffness of the alpha-actinin LINKER between two cortex nodes, an elastic element with the bond's rest at the built distance. FERRER MISREAD CORRECTED: the former 4.6e5 ('455 pN/nm, Ferrer 2008 AFM') is Ferrer 2008 PNAS 105:9221 (10.1073/pnas.0706124105, SE119 OK; optical tweezers, not AFM) Hummer-Szabo fit k_BT*kappa_m = 455 +/- 215 pN/nm — the curvature of the actin-ABP BOND's energy well over x‡ 0.28 nm, not the 35-nm rod's stiffness; no direct measurement of the intact rod's axial stiffness exists (EXAMPLE). Two bounds put the value here: (i) self-consistency with crosslink.k_off0 — the resting thermal load sqrt(k_BT k) must be << f_char = k_BT/x_beta, i.e. k << f_char^2/k_BT = 5.7e4 pN/um (at 4.6e5 every bond carried 44 pN rms at rest, Bell x17, and 58 % tore in 10 us on RESULT-2026-09-11-motor-occupancy); (ii) the step — a 4.4-nm thermal kick at dt 1e-6 must not push the Bell exponent past 1: k <= 3.5e3. Molecule: 8 spectrin repeats per rod, folded-repeat stiffness ~1700 pN/nm each (Paramore 2005 MD), flexible terminal regions (Golji 2009), and the repeats UNFOLD at 25-35 pN (Rief 1999 JMB 286:553) below the 40-80 pN bond rupture. DESIGN ITEM (PI 17:11): the crosslink as a YIELDING element — this stiffness up to f_y ~25-35 pN, then ~30 nm of unfolded extension per repeat, refolding < 1 s on release (a bonds/builder change); until then this elastic element is the stand-in | independent of erm.k: alpha-actinin linker vs ezrin linker; same value 4600 (arp23.k is bound to crosslink.k). 10.1073/pnas.0706124105

spec.example.toml · range

cell5.0uM1.0–5.0swept
crosslink.molecular_model

PI-BATCH-2016 (2026-10-07 20:16 KST, lane cell-structure-1007) A12: ON by default (the two-arm MOLECULE; the owner-node idiom 0 is the DECLARED COMPARISON ARM). With 1 the molecules' arms bind every live actin part (crosslinker_molecules.ACTIN_PARTS: cortex, cortex_arp23, cytoplasm_actin, ...), which extends alpha-actinin past the formin cortex and filamin past cytoplasm_actin (the 10-07 re-audit: 77.5 % of cortex mass was uncrosslinked). KNOWN LIMIT carried by the default: material_site_overrides is still unconsumed by a kernel, so an arm addresses the NEARER node of its site's segment (<= half a segment, 0.025 um at resolution.spacing 0.05; INVENTORY-2026-09-21 E' X1). Before A12: WHICH crosslinker representation the build uses, and the ONE row that chooses it. 0 = the incumbent owner-node idiom (the crosslinker is a relation owned by a filament node; cell/bonds.build_kinds). 1 = the finite two-arm MOLECULE of codex/bio-wiring-20260915 (cell/build/crosslinkers.build_two_arm_crosslinker): a massive freely hinged centre node per molecule, two independent arms of length/2 and stiffness 2k, population = conc x actual cytoplasm volume. The two are different physics, not a refactor: the owner-node idiom cannot represent a 0.16 um rod whose capture radius is smaller than its own length without every bond being born compressed, and the two-arm model has no such defect; the molecule model in turn needs the material-site machinery on the device before its arms bind exact monomer sites rather than segment endpoints. Default 0 until one device run compares them. Companion rows (<prefix>.molecular_weight, .radius, .arm_reach) are read only at 1.

switch, not a material value (lane G2 2026-10-13; PI decision 2026-10-13 22:32 item 7: the crosslinker rod gets a hinge law, its stiffness rows SWEPT and unsourced where no source exists): 1 = a two-arm crosslinker molecule with BOTH arms bound on two different nodes (molecule.distinct_arm_partners = 1) carries one bending row (partner A, centre, partner B) of the world's triple law, E = (alpha/2)(|x_A - 2 x_c + x_B| - s0)^2, s0 = length cos(hinge_angle/2), alpha = hinge_k_theta / ((length/2) sin(hinge_angle/2))^2 (build/crosslinkers.hinge_law), and the equilibrium build's centre and joint arm draws carry its Boltzmann factor on the two-arm state (build/equilibrium.py, HINGE). 0 or absent = no angle law at the centre: the build of candidate 18d878a25 bit for bit (a 35 nm rod folded at its middle bridges node pairs 8-33 nm apart). RUNTIME LIMITATION, recorded in the part's arm_build: the row follows its two arm relations while both hold the partners it was built on; a pair formed at runtime carries no hinge row and the attach weight does not read the hinge energy.

power-stroke step 5.5 nm, Veigel 2003 (carried via Clausen 2017 Table 1). Read for its MAGNITUDE since W14 (DESIGN-2026-10-01-motor-walk-step §3.2; PI 2026-09-30 21:12 decision 39): with crossbridge.site_period in the file it is the lever stride, the distance a stroke moves the relation's anchor along the actin while the head keeps its site (the node walk read its sign only). Measured NM2 steps: Hundt 2016 Sci Rep 6:20554 (10.1038/srep20554, SE582 source_audit OK), NM-2A-HMM single molecule, 'a mean forward step size of 5.0 +/- 1.6 nm and a mean backward step size of 4.7 +/- 1.9 nm', and 'the mean values above underestimate the step sizes by approximately 10-20%'; Norstrom 2010 J Biol Chem 285:26326 (10.1074/jbc.M110.123851, SE583 source_audit OK), NM2B, 'a forward displacement of 5.4 nm and, surprisingly, frequent backward steps of -5.9 nm' (backward steps are later rows, PI decision 46). Range: Hundt's 5.0 nm as measured to 5.0/0.8 = 6.25 nm (his 20 % correction) — a proposal; Norstrom's 5.4 and Veigel's 5.5 lie inside | independent of crossbridge.site_period: two different lattices/lengths (attach-site period vs power-stroke step) that happen to read 5.5 nm. 10.1038/srep20554

PI A4 2026-08-29: the stroke walks the partner chain; +1 = ascending chain index. MEANING at sites (W14, PI 2026-09-30 21:12 decision 39): with crossbridge.site_period in the file the stroke's direction along the arc is stroke_sign x the partner chain's declared polarity (world.chain_polarity: +1 where next points to the barbed end), so +1 = toward the barbed end; myosin II is barbed-end directed — SOURCED once a KB row carries it. Without the row (the node walk) it reads as before

crossbridge.site_period

the crossbridge's attach lattice along actin — its PRESENCE turns the site crossbridge on (#56 (a-ii) lever shift, DESIGN-2026-10-01-motor-walk-step §3.2; PI 2026-09-30 21:12 decisions 39-43: 0.0055 um EXAMPLE, its own lattice, occupied start at sites; without the row the crossbridge binds and walks at nodes). Two actin subunit rises, i.e. one long-pitch strand's protomer repeat (27.5 A rise, von der Ecken 2015 Nature as carried in crosslink.site_period's source). 0.00275 = every subunit; 0.0365 = the azimuth-limited half-pitch the crosslinkers use. An actin property plus head accessibility (the model has no azimuth): a PI row. Under the lever shift it is independent of the stroke (crossbridge.stroke is the stride). The site crossbridge's partners are the actin populations with an accepted polarity only (decision 42 as corrected 22:4x: sf_arc and stress_fiber, whose builders declare no polarity, are out until polarity rows exist; cell/bonds.CROSSBRIDGE_SITE_PARTNERS)

crossbridge.k_adp_release

PI signature 2026-09-11 11:26 (Lead transcript 14373ea7; KB-2026-09-11-crossbridge-rates.md). ISOFORM ERROR CORRECTED: the former 0.35/s is NMIIB's unloaded ADP release (Kovacs 2007 Table 1: NM2B single-headed 0.38 +/- 0.09, HMM 0.27 +/- 0.06; Wang 2003). NMIIA — the engine's motor (hand_kmc.NMIIA_MYOSIN; x_adp derived for 2A) — is k0 = 2.7 +/- 0.3/s (single-headed, = Kovacs 2003 JBC 278:38132, 10.1074/jbc.M305453200, SE550 OK) / 2.9 +/- 1.0 (HMM); Stam 2015 carries 1.71/s from Kovacs 2003 -> spread: 1.7-2.9/s (lognormal prior, factor 1.3). Kovacs 2007 PNAS 104:9994 (doi 10.1073/pnas.0701181104, PMID 17548820, SE424 OK): resisting load slows it 5x (2A: 2.9 -> 0.59) / 12x (2B), assisting load speeds it 4x (11/s) — the load factors and x_adp were already 2A's, only the base rate was 2B's. Formerly: resisting load slows it 5x (2A) / 12x (2B) at ~2 pN, assisting load speeds it 4x. READ by bonds._crossbridge as the stroked state's detachment (2026-09-06, KB-2026-09-06 §4.8/§7.1b: unbound from the SWEPT k_off0). KB: SE424 Kovacs2007_PNAS, source_audit OK 2026-09-06 12:0x (key repaired from the encoding-stripped Kovcs2007; audit re-run). Spread: the paper gives ~0.35 /s (one significant figure), read as a factor of 1.4 either way 10.1074/jbc.M305453200

cell0.271/s0.135–0.54sweptmeasured
actin_chem.monomer_rise

2.7 nm axial rise per subunit — the growth stroke delta (physics.end_growth), Popov 2016 p15 (KB SE285) citing Splettstoesser 2011 (10.1002/prot.23017); SOURCED on registration of Splettstoesser 2011 (KB-2026-09-07-medyan-chemistry §10 #7). cytoplasm_actin.py's SUBUNITS_PER_UM = 370 is this same rise as a count DECLARED SUB-SPACING EXCEPTION (RES-UNIFY; PI 2026-10-09 15:20 AUTO-1009-ALL, D1 decided by the Lead under it; the nmii lever row is the precedent): with CoreOptions.growth_tip = tail (physics/tip_tail.py, DESIGN-2026-10-09-tip-refinement-and-monomer-oracle) a growing end's last units are nodes spaced at THIS rise — rows of rest delta (the odd first piece in [delta, 2 delta), the end slot in (delta, 2 delta]) — coarsened into resolution.spacing rows every round(spacing/delta) units. The tail is made at bind, not by a builder, so the build census (_build_check.check_uniform) never sees it; the run record's tail channels count it 10.1002/prot.23017

actin_chem.chain_death

switch row, not a measurement: 1 = an actin filament that depolymerises to its last body unit LEAVES THE WORLD (physics/end_growth _die: its 3 nodes to the family pool, its chain record free for a later birth or cut, its last contour Sum rest / delta returned to the pool as units) — PI AUTO-1009-ALL decision 1 'a chain whose last body unit depolymerises retires'. 0 = the incumbent floor (counted 'floor', the chain kept at 3 nodes). Held 0 until the A1 unit world verifies it on a device (PENDING_DEFAULT_FLIPS id chain-death); refused with unit chemistry on (its dissolve is not written) | range: a switch

spec.example.toml · range

cell010–1example
actin_chem.dual_mass

switch row, not a measurement (B11, assembly2-1009; DESIGN-2026-10-09 §1 B11 / NOTE-2026-10-07 G3): 1 = every live growing chain's node masses are its family's built linear density x each node's dual length (half of every adjacent rest), rewritten after every topology event and stroke (physics/growth_wiring _dual_mass_kernel), so a born, grown, cut or shrunk chain carries the mass its contour holds; 0 = masses as built and never redistributed (the incumbent: a pool node keeps rho pi r^2 L, a stroke moves no mass). The momentum of the mass a stroke adds is the well-mixed pool's (zero), not conserved per node. Held 0 until A1 verifies it (PENDING_DEFAULT_FLIPS id dual-mass) | range: a switch

spec.example.toml · range

cell010–1example
actin_chem.spontaneous_nucleation

switch row, not a measurement (B10, assembly arm): 1 = factor-free nucleation in the cytoplasm — the trimer-nucleus flux k_on c^3 / (actin_chem.dimer_kd x actin_chem.trimer_kd) [uM/s] (k_on = actin_chem.k_on_barbed_atp at the cell temperature, c the free ATP-actin), wakes a 3-node chain of the formin family at one of actin_chem.spontaneous_site_count volume points (physics/chain_birth kind 2). Default 0: with profilin/thymosin buffering the free ATP-actin near 1 uM the flux is negligible, and the arm is declared so it can be measured, not assumed away (PARALLEL-TRACKS) | range: a switch

spec.example.toml · range

cell0.0011/s1e-05–0.1swept
actin_chem.cofilin_decorated_fraction

the fraction of built filament subunits carrying cofilin. THIS ROW STANDS IN FOR BINDING KINETICS THAT ARE NOT WIRED: no cofilin binding row exists in this file (nor on codex/bio-wiring-20260915, whose cofilin path is a 64-row molecular G/F preparation that is not ported), so the decoration cannot be computed from the file and is DECLARED. Sized from stoichiometry and from what cofilin does in a resting cell, not from any gate: one cofilin per actin protomer against actin_chem.cofilin_conc 20 uM and the filament this spec builds puts the hard ceiling at 0.0987 on the shipped build (1.021e7 molecules against 1.035e8 built protomers; cell/severing.decorated_fraction_ceiling recomputes it from the BUILT protomer count and refuses anything above it, with both counts in the message); and most cofilin in a resting cell is Ser3-phosphorylated and cannot bind F-actin at all, so the resting decoration sits well under that ceiling. 0.05 is an order-of-magnitude EXAMPLE inside it and a PI-GAP inference target, not a measurement. WARNING the real law (Kadzik 2026, aleph/laws/cofilin_severing.py) severs at decorated/bare BOUNDARIES and peaks at INTERMEDIATE decoration, while the uniform-rate form this row feeds is monotone in it — no run may claim the occupancy dependence. not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED

spec.example.toml · range

cell0.0510.0–1.0swept
actin_chem.severing_reserve_fraction

spare CHAIN records per built chain, because a cut makes two chains of one and the chain count is fixed at construction (the same device as <pop>.dormant_fraction for nodes). A VALUE computed at authoring time, not tuned (PI 2026-09-29 decision 12: kept valued, source rewritten): cofilin_severing_rate 0.01 /(um.s) x cofilin_decorated_fraction 0.05 x a 3.0 um filament contour (the single cortex contour of the pre-split build; no row since 2026-09-24) = 1.5e-3 cuts per chain per second, so a 100 s horizon (a declared number, not a row) needs 0.15 records per chain and 0.5 carries that with 3.3x headroom. A run that outlives it SATURATES and the step is counted (physics/chain_split no_record), never raised. Each record costs two dead segment rows and NO node. not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED

arp23.conc

Arp2/3 complex ~1-2 uM (Pollard 2000). PI-GAP. not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED. g3-arp-pool-1013 (PI 2026-10-13 22:32 item 11): this row is the TOTAL complex concentration, not the free one (the source line states the whole-cell amount, as the tubulin and actin totals do; form = concentration, conserved). Under arp23.pool_ledger = 1 (default) the free pool at the start is this total minus the complexes held by the BUILT junctions (by count, over the row's declared built measure); arp23.pool_ledger = 0 reads it as the free pool and every built junction carries one more complex on top (the build before)

spec.example.toml · range

cell2.0uM1.0–2.0swept
arp23.pool_ledger

g3-arp-pool-1013 (PI 2026-10-13 22:32 item 11, as relayed by the Lead; lane F7 measured the consequence): DECLARED ARM, an accounting rule and not a rate. 1 (default) = arp23.conc is the TOTAL complex concentration; the bath's free ARP23 count at the start = total count - complexes held by the built junctions (in-part branch junctions and formin roots, which now return theirs on debranch), the count over the row's declared built measure; a world whose built junctions exceed the declared total is NOT clamped silently: the Core refuses it as the build-ledger departure pool_overdrawn (declared / built / deficit per species) unless CoreOptions.allow_departures names it, then the free pool is 0. 0 = arp23.conc is the free pool and each built junction carries one more complex on top, bit for bit the build before. F7 (host, native arithmetic): total 2 uM steady state 1.015 x the built junction count, free 2 uM in a closed pool 1.94 x. On ladder-size worlds the built junctions exceed the total (U1 R = 1 um: 9,421 built vs 5,042 total at 2 uM in that volume) and the world is refused. The nucleation reserve (cell/nucleation.sites_needed) sizes from the same total (pool = total - bound)

arp23.nucleation_reserve_fraction

nucleation SITES per built Arp2/3 chain (ceil(this x chains) dormant junction relations, each with a mother node, a frame and its two dead junction angle rows); the chain RECORDS the reserve holds are sites x arp23.nucleation_records_per_site, derived from the run length (2026-10-07, NOTE-2026-10-07-chain-birth-admission; before, one record per site). RE-ENABLED at the lane's 0.1 (2026-10-07): it shipped at 0 from 2026-09-21 (device, RunPod A100, 353b9c858: births on, woken daughters 6.8e3 -> 3.8e5 -> 1.2e6 pN in five steps, all-on cell non-finite at k = 3) because a born chain was outside the integrate path's axial-constraint workspace; the 2026-09-22 registry (physics/chain_registry, device software tests 9/9 job-n2uf00wv72md on fab2bef1c) admits it there, and 2026-10-07 admits it to the energy core's junction angle rows, chord and contact-barrier queries. NO NATIVE RUN WITH BIRTHS ON SINCE 09-21 — the native discriminator (outputs/physics/ct_overnight_20260922/native_birth_inputs) was never launched. The site count is a DISCRETISATION, not a rate: the world's propensity is k_b0 x N_free x n_free/n_sites (cell/nucleation), exact only while sites are free. At native (1.33e6 Arp2/3 chains, 1.33e5 sites, k_b0 x N_free = 0.037 /s x 1.46e6 = 5.4e4 /s) the sites fill in ~2.5 s and nucleation is then site-limited (debranch 0.003 /s x sites = 400 /s): sizing sites from the ceiling over sim.reserve_horizon would be ~1.2 per chain (PI decision, NOTE §3). Each site costs one bond row and two triple rows; each record two dead segment rows and three pool nodes (build/cortex adds them). not in KB source_audit — register before SOURCED

arp23.nucleation_reserve_rule

f7-arp23-1013 (AUDIT2-C H6, 2026-10-13; the Lead's instruction: derive the reserve from the declared run and the rate rows, refuse a reserve that cannot cover it): DECLARED ARM, a sizing rule and not a rate. 1 (default) = the nucleation SITES are the junctions born and still held at the end of the declared run, ceil(L(T)), L(t) = (pool + built) k_b / (k_b + k_d) (1 - exp(-(k_b + k_d) t)) - built (exp(-k_d t) - exp(-(k_b + k_d) t)), k_b = arp23.nucleation_rate, k_d = arp23.debranch_rate, T = sim.reserve_horizon, pool = arp23.conc over its built measure, built = the built in-part junctions (cell/nucleation.sites_needed). arp23.nucleation_reserve_fraction is then only the on/off declaration (0 = no nucleation). 0 = ceil(fraction x chains), the build before the lane; the Core then refuses the world when that is fewer than the run needs (class nucleation_reserve_exhausted). An expectation, not a quantile; the site discretisation still throttles the rate as sites fill (the exact cure, renormalising the coefficient by the live free-site count, is not built). Host P05: 1,885 sites (rule 0) -> 2,553 (rule 1). NATIVE: the count becomes ~0.65 x pool — a memory decision the fraction row's source left to the PI

arp23.branch_angle_max

f7-arp23-1013 (Lead 2026-10-13, after the first device run of arp23.junction_rule = 1 died at Core construction: 'a declared Arp2/3 junction row is collinear at its declared angle'): the UPPER bound of the branch-angle draw (build.cortex.branch_angle_draw: built daughters and nucleation sites), by rejection. Cause of the refusal: 52 of 37,684 declared rows on U1 / C03 (26 of 18,842 on P05) belonged to daughters drawn past 90 deg, whose row stored pi/2 + theta > 180 deg (fixed: build.cortex.junction_interior stores the row's own interior angle); and draws NEAR 90 deg are rows the term holds only through a diverging stiffness — with the fold alone P05 carried 13 junction rows above 1e6 pN/um, the worst 2.4e9, against 1.4e4 for the stiffest junction row of the pre-1013 as-built rest. 84 = arp23.branch_angle + 2 x arp23.branch_angle_sd at the shipped rows, where the converted stiffness (1.8e4 pN/um) is that of the pre-1013 build's worst row: the lane's pick, a model bound on what the three-node junction term can carry, NOT a measured cutoff — it removes 2.3 % of a 70 +/- 7 draw (realised sd 6.6). PI DECISION: the bound, or a junction term that is regular at 90 deg (a two-direction angle term, physics.energy.pairangle) so no bound is needed. 180 = the unbounded l6 draw. g1-junction-1013: NOT READ when arp23.junction_angle_form = 1 (the two-direction angle element has no collinear row: the draw is then the declared law on (0, 180) deg)
